classification.difficultyReason: Translate the opposite-side observation points into two right triangles, calculate each horizontal distance using tangent and recognise that the distances must be added.

content.prompt: The angles of elevation of the top of a tower $T$, $120\text{ m}$ high, from two points $P$ and $Q$ on opposite sides of it were measured as $60^\circ$ and $45^\circ$ respectively. Find the distance from $P$ to $Q$ correct to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
Let $F$ be the foot of the tower. The horizontal distances add because $P$ and $Q$ lie on opposite sides.
$$\begin{align*}PF&=\frac{120}{\tan60^\circ}\\QF&=\frac{120}{\tan45^\circ}\\PQ&=PF+QF\\PQ&=\frac{120}{\tan60^\circ}+\frac{120}{\tan45^\circ}\\PQ&\approx189.3\text{ m}\quad\text{(1 decimal place).}\end{align*}$$
